clue.text: Orchestrate popular march to accommodate the troops

parts.note: popular means in, as in fashion

indicators.note: to accommodate means one piece takes the other in, housing it within itself

parts.note: to strut is to march proudly
the troops are the men

explanation.surface: A conductor arranges a popular march to play to the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestrate' looks like an instruction but is the definition, a verb meaning to score music for players; 'to accommodate' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To instrument a piece is to score it for the instruments of a band, a verb sense close to orchestrate.

clue.text: Self-confessed Black-foot?

parts.note: I am is what a person says when confessing who or what they are
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A member of the Blackfoot people admits their identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blackfoot' looks like the Native American people; split it and 'foot' is a metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one short and one long syllable, the basic unit of English verse.

clue.text: Mark hearing aid

indicators.note: hearing says the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a mark is a gullible victim, a sucker

explanation.surface: Notice the device that helps a deaf person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is a con artist's victim, SUCKER; 'hearing' says the answer sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Help given in time of need, a synonym of aid.

clue.text: Special occasion for a Russian landlord on the Sabbath, perhaps

indicators.note: on puts the landlord above the day in this down answer

parts.note: red stood for Soviet Russian, from the communist flag
a landlord is one who lets property
the Sabbath is one example of a day

explanation.surface: A Soviet property owner's Sunday is a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A LETTER, read literally, is one who lets property; 'on' places it above DAY in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Important dates were printed in red on church calendars, hence a memorable, special day.

clue.text: Single college in exclusive possession

parts.note: mono means single or one
poly is short for polytechnic, a type of British college

explanation.surface: One college has sole ownership of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A POLY was a British polytechnic, a higher-education college.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole control of a market or commodity, owned by one party alone.

clue.text: Real organization in the city? Not quite!

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York, the city

indicators.note: organization means the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is there a real company in town? Almost!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite!' is the whole definition, exclamation and all; 'organization' signals the rearrangement and 'in' the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost but not entirely, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Left on board long ago, the animal has gone fat

indicators.note: has gone says the animal's letters disappear from the longer word

parts.note: larboard is the old sailors' word for the port, or left-hand, side of a ship
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: An old ship's port side, with its creature departed, is greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: LARBOARD, the term that 'port' replaced, loses the wild pig BOAR to leave the cooking fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: A thickhead to provoke an attack

parts.note: the head of thick is its first letter
to tempt someone is to provoke or entice them

explanation.surface: Someone stupid tries to goad another into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thickhead' splits into thick plus head, the first letter of thick.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt on someone's life is an attack on it; the word also means an assault or bid.

clue.text: 20 groups debate about missing graduate

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes round the groups
missing says the graduate's letters are absent from the word

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
genera are biological groups, the plural of genus

explanation.surface: Groups argue about a graduate who is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: '20' stands for the answer to 20 across. 'missing' removes the graduate and 'about' wraps what remains of the debate round the groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who has fallen into moral decline.

clue.text: Two men on the staff of a Greek Division

indicators.note: on puts the two men after the staff, attached to its end

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
Don is a man's name
Ian is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two officers serve on the staff of a Greek army division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' attaches the two names after the staff; 'Two men' supplies both names from one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is a region of northern Greece, so the adjective describes something from that division of the country.

clue.text: A contribution to host a get together for the boys

indicators.note: A contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help host a men-only party.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in the last letters of 'host', takes 'a', and ends with the first letter of 'get', which also starts the printed 'get-together'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a men-only gathering, typically before a wedding.

clue.text: Historic tax on old money, in line with the law in Westminster

indicators.note: on puts the tax ahead of the money

parts.note: scot was a medieval tax, as in scot-free
L for libra was the pound in pre-decimal British money
and means with
a yard is a measuring line of three feet

explanation.surface: An old levy on old currency is in step with legal rules in Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT survives in 'scot-free', meaning untaxed; L is the pound of pre-decimal money. AND comes with the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: The headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, so metonymically the police force of the capital.

clue.text: Harbour a spy

definitions.meaning: a stone breakwater or pier enclosing a harbour
an agent planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A port shelters a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour wall is called a breakwater or pier of that name; a spy planted long-term inside an organisation is called by the same word.

clue.text: Officer in charge in, for instance. North Island.

indicators.note: the second in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the North is one example of a pole
IC is the standard short form of in charge, the phrase the word completes with the in before it
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An officer is in command in, say, a northern island.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to 'in charge'; the second is the insertion signal. North is one example of a POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer.

clue.text: Compensating for disappointing scenery

parts.note: a performance that is off is below par, disappointing
a stage setting is its scenery

explanation.surface: Making up for drab stage scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: To balance one thing against another is to make up for it, so counterbalancing.

clue.text: Anticipate warning order

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
to tell someone to do something is to order it

explanation.surface: Expect a command that comes with a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the warning shouted on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict something is to anticipate it before it happens.

clue.text: Money once enough for treats

indicators.note: enough for suggests the letters of the word that follows are all the raw material needed, rearranged

explanation.surface: Coins of the past were enough to buy sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: TREATS is rearranged; 'enough for' says those letters suffice to build the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece, so currency of long ago.

clue.text: Badly garbled direction to raise capital

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put in a poor, disordered arrangement

parts.note: E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Muddled instructions for raising funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges GARBLED to BELGRAD, then E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Serbia, formerly of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: He was dethroned, by Jove!

parts.note: reads as a mild oath, but literally names the Roman god who overthrew his own father and took the throne of heaven

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a monarch has been deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By Jove!' is an old-fashioned exclamation, but here it means 'by Jupiter': the king of the gods deposed his father.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth the father of Jupiter ruled the gods until his son overthrew him.

clue.text: Flood unearths gold in the river

indicators.note: in places the gold within the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A deluge turns up gold in the riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unearths' is a link; 'in' signals the containment. Heraldic gold is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rush of water, a flood.

clue.text: Declining a dip at the end of the month

indicators.note: at the end of puts the two pieces after the month's abbreviation

parts.note: Dec is short for December
a dent is a dip in a surface

explanation.surface: A drop in income arrives as the month ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of' places the dip and its article after the month; the definition is an adjective, describing a society in moral decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A decadent society is in moral decline, falling from its former standards.

clue.text: A care he concealed in pain

indicators.note: concealed suggests the letters of the phrase are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: A worry he kept hidden while suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' disguises A CARE HE by rearranging its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain felt in the ear, a specific kind of ache.

clue.text: The foreign chap 'as fallen from the conveyor

indicators.note: fallen from says those letters drop out of the longer word

parts.note: an assignor is one who conveys property or rights to another in law
'as is a dropped-aitch has, read as the two letters

explanation.surface: A foreigner tumbled off a moving belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveyor' suggests a belt, but here is the legal sense: an ASSIGNOR conveys property. Drop AS from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a man, equivalent to Mr or sir.

clue.text: Passing through an obsession about study

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Getting past a fixation on learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the obsession wraps round the study; 'Passing through' is how a needle is loaded with cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton strand going through the eye of a needle is said to be doing this, so it means passing through.

clue.text: Right inside a monk's cramped sleeping quarters

indicators.note: inside puts the letter for right within the monk's title

parts.note: Dom is the title given to Benedictine monks

explanation.surface: A monk's sleeping cell has only just enough room.
explanation.walkthrough: Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk, as in Dom Perignon.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for dormitory, a shared room of many beds packed close together.

clue.text: Detail that is in the Roman calendar

indicators.note: detail read as de-tail, removing the last letter

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated ie

explanation.surface: A fine point about dates in the ancient Roman calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' splits as de-tail, cutting the final T from ID EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle day of a Roman month, a date in that calendar.

clue.text: News, perhaps, originating in the established media

indicators.note: originating points to the letters where each of the next four words begins

explanation.surface: A story that began in the mainstream press.
explanation.definitionFit: A news report is one piece, a single article in a list of stories.

clue.text: Deranged, perhaps, and unable to get about inside

indicators.note: inside puts the abbreviation for about within the rearranged letters
perhaps hints the letters of the two words beside it could form something else

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone mentally disturbed and unable to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deranged' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition; 'perhaps' rearranges AND UNABLE, and 'to get about inside' adds C within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mentally unstable is described as having lost their balance, so deranged.

clue.text: Old German seized Hanover first

parts.note: to have got something is to have seized it

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the city name

explanation.surface: A German of old captured Hanover before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were a Germanic people who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Day lasting too long to be abandoned

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
something interminable seems to go on without end

explanation.surface: A day that drags on so long it feels deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forsaken by all has no companions left.
